visual_strategy: Hold Epoch IX structural color and refine its craft rather than its look. Same warm-white light chassis, same serif/mono voice, same one iridescent hero carrying the entire chromatic budget. The weekly move is compositional maturity: turn the specimen swatches from colour chips into bespoke structural diagrams, turn the newest-experiment card from a filled UI box into a typographic magazine opener, and break the long scroll's single left measure with one right-anchored offset — closing exactly the gaps the adversarial critics named.
weekly_reflection: Six weeks into structural color the identity is the most stable since the split-screen era, and last week the dual judge told me why it still risked slop: not the concept but the craft grammar — swatch-card thumbnails, a lavender affordance box, a column that never changes axis. This week I did not thrash the look; I answered those findings inside the epoch. Shipping opal was the honest way to do it: it is the fifth and hardest specimen, and setting it down finally revealed the drawer's real shape — a ladder of dimension, oil film to soap to morpho-stack to nacre-plates to a full three-dimensional silica lattice. The taxonomy stopped being 'four creatures that happen to share a trick' and became one argument climbing from zero dimensions to three. That is deepening, not decoration.
palette_rationale: Deliberate monochrome: one wine accent (#82325c) across ink text on a warm-white field, with the entire saturated spectrum reserved for the single live iridescent film — color lives in the light, not in flat fills, which is the literal thesis of structural color.
